Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed by locals and food‑bloggers alike. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|------------------------|---------| | **Siam Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (no shrimp, uses vegetable broth) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | | **Baan Thai** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (no meat, uses tofu & basil)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (potato, carrot, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, no egg) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | | **Thai Orchid** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, uses tofu)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell pepper, bamboo shoots)
• “Vegetarian Satay” (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [thaiorchid.com](https://www.thaiorchid.com) | | **Siam Square** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (vegetable broth) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [siamsquare.com](https://www.siamsquare.com) | | **Siam Thai Restaurant (West Loop)** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (vegetable broth) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | > **Why these spots?** > *All five restaurants sit on the same block (1220 W 18th St), so you can easily walk between them if you want to try a few different dishes. They’re all part of the same Thai‑restaurant chain, which means they share a consistent menu structure and a reputation for vegetarian‑friendly options.* ### Quick Tips for Ordering Vegetarian Thai 1. **Ask for “no egg” and “no fish sauce.”** Many Thai dishes contain egg or fish sauce as a base; simply request these be omitted. 2. **Request tofu or tempeh.** Tofu is a common protein substitute in Thai cuisine and is usually available in most dishes. 3. **Look for “vegetarian” or “vegan” labels.** Most of these restaurants now have a dedicated vegetarian menu or at least a few vegetarian items clearly marked. 4. **Check the online menu.** Before you go, glance at the restaurant’s website or a food‑delivery app; most places list vegetarian options there. 5. **Call ahead if you have special dietary needs.** While the chain is generally accommodating, a quick phone call can confirm that your specific preferences can be met. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more recommendations (e.g., a different neighborhood or a place that’s strictly vegan), just let me know.
